findings.detail: Core text.split LF retains the terminal empty item, contrary to actual native read_file producer which pops it when the file ends LF. One-line needle\n yields hint end_line=2 while native read_file returns end_line=total_lines=1. Existing test expects the incorrect extra line.
findings.reproduction: Actual temporary Git repository plus createRepositoryTools read_file; hint_end=2, native_end=1, native_total=1. No provider calls.
findings.required_correction: Additively mirror native LF extent and test trailing LF, CRLF, no terminal LF, empty file and last-line match via the actual producer.

checks: All 12 supplied unit tests independently pass; they do not catch the LF mismatch.
Reviewed normalization, per-file df/path postings, atomic budget exclusion and subsequent sorted stop, disjoint windows, deterministic quantized scores and whole-hint response reduction.
Hints expose location/revision/hash/rank only; response shape alone does not prove native no-credit integration.
limitations: No resource worker, Git inventory producer, process isolation or native adapter is implemented in this core.

Native source reader currently caps files at 2000000 bytes, below the index 8MiB eligibility cap. Future integration must disclose unreadable indexed files or explicitly resolve this protocol compatibility; no silent source-reader change.

Native read_file additionally rejects returned UTF-8 spans above 32768 bytes. A 40-line hint is not necessarily readable; a single oversized line cannot be rescued by reducing line_count. Explicit accessibility policy and tests remain an integration prerequisite.
No quality, token-saving or live-admission claim.
